# dodopayments_meter (Resource)

Manages a meter. The API does not delete this object. When Terraform destroys the resource, the provider archives the object.

!> **Destroy behavior:** The API does not delete this object. When Terraform destroys the resource, the provider archives the object. To restore the object, use the `dodopayments_meter_unarchive` action.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "dodopayments_meter" "example" {
  aggregation = {
    type = "count"
  }
  event_name       = "example-meter"
  measurement_unit = "example-meter"
  name             = "example-meter"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `aggregation` (Attributes) Aggregation configuration for the meter. A change to this value destroys the resource and creates a new resource. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--aggregation))
- `event_name` (String) Event name to track. A change to this value destroys the resource and creates a new resource.
- `measurement_unit` (String) measurement unit.
- `name` (String) Name of the meter.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Optional description of the meter.
- `filter` (Attributes) Optional filter to apply to the meter. A change to this value destroys the resource and creates a new resource. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--filter))

### Read-Only

- `business_id` (String)
- `created_at` (String)
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `updated_at` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--aggregation"></a>
### Nested Schema for `aggregation`

Required:

- `type` (String) Aggregation type for the meter.

Optional:

- `key` (String) Required when type is not COUNT. If you remove this attribute from the configuration, the API keeps the last value.


<a id="nestedatt--filter"></a>
### Nested Schema for `filter`

Required:

- `clauses` (String) Filter clauses - can be direct conditions or nested filters (up to 3 levels deep). A JSON document. Use `jsonencode()` to set it.
- `conjunction` (String) Logical conjunction to apply between clauses (and/or).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = dodopayments_meter.example
  identity = {
    id = "<id>"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) The ID of the meter.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = dodopayments_meter.example
  id = "<id>"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a meter by its ID.
terraform import dodopayments_meter.example <id>
```
